title: Etale linearization of a regular immersion
statement:
In the fixed purity setting [def-pur-conventions], let $k$ be the perfect ground field and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion of pure codimension $c\geq1$ as in [def-pur-regular-immersion]; in particular $X$ and $Z$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Assume $X$ is smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $Z$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then:

1. $Z$ is smooth over $k$.
2. For every $z\in Z$, put $m=\dim_z Z$, the dimension of the smooth component through $z$ [def-kun-dimension]. There are etale neighbourhoods $U\to X$ of $i(z)$ and $V\to Z$ of $z$, an etale $k$-morphism $u:U\to\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space], and an identification
$$V=Z\times_XU=u^{-1}(\mathbf A^m_k),$$
where $\mathbf A^m_k\subseteq\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$ is the coordinate subspace $x_1=\cdots=x_c=0$ and the inverse image is scheme-theoretic [def-pc-base-change]. The restriction $u|_V:V\to\mathbf A^m_k$ is etale, and the ideal of $V$ in $U$ is generated by $u^*x_1,\ldots,u^*x_c$.

proof.text: The field $k$ throughout is the fixed algebraic closure of $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ named in [def-pur-conventions]. The finite-type and regularity hypotheses on $Z$ and the perfectness of $k$ are precisely those in [sk-lem-regular-smooth], so $a_Z=a_X\circ i:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. This proves clause 1. Fix any point $z\in Z$ and put $x=i(z)$; all the following constructions take place around this point, without assuming that it is closed.

Choose a finite-type affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$ containing $x$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The closed immersion identifies $Z\cap W$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ for an ideal $J$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field). Thus $J$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $\mathfrak p$ be the prime of $x$, and identify $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}=A_{\mathfrak p}$, $S=\mathcal O_{Z,z}=R/J_{\mathfrak p}$ and $I=J_{\mathfrak p}=\ker(R\twoheadrightarrow S)$. At $x$, [def-pur-regular-immersion] supplies a length-$c$ regular generating sequence $r_1,\ldots,r_c$ of $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], its classes are a basis of $J_{\mathfrak p}/J_{\mathfrak p}^2$. Represent $r_i=f_i/s_i$ with $f_i\in J$ and $s_i\notin\mathfrak p$. Replacing each class by the unit multiple $s_ir_i$ preserves this basis. The finite module $J/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ has zero localization at $\mathfrak p$: choose finitely many generators, and for each choose an annihilator outside $\mathfrak p$. Invert the product of these annihilators and the $s_i$. On the resulting principal open neighbourhood the $f_i$ generate $J$. The isomorphism $S^{\oplus c}\cong I/I^2$ at $z$ sends the standard basis to their classes; tensoring it with $\kappa(z)$ gives a basis of $(I/I^2)\otimes_S\kappa(z)$. This writes out the shrinking argument rather than assuming that stalk generation is global.

source.place: first paragraph, choice of ideal generators; second paragraph, shrinking to keep them generating

proof.text: The smooth rank theorem [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension], applied to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at $z$, makes the cotangent fibre $\Omega_{Z/k,z}\otimes\kappa(z)$ $m$-dimensional, with $m=\dim_zZ$. On an affine neighbourhood it is generated by differentials of functions: this is the generator-and-relation construction of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], read in the relative sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]; [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies these with the differentials of the germs. Select $m$ differentials of germs from this spanning family whose images form a basis. Represent the finitely many germs by functions on a common principal open of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ around $z$; lifting its denominator to $A$ and inverting it shrinks the ambient affine neighbourhood as well. Lift the resulting functions $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ through the quotient of the localized rings $A\twoheadrightarrow A/J$. The exact conormal fibre sequence [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion] sends the $c$ conormal basis vectors of step 2 to $df_1,\ldots,df_c$. Hence $df_1,\ldots,df_c,dg_1,\ldots,dg_m$ is a basis of the ambient cotangent fibre: project a linear relation to the quotient to kill the $g_j$ coefficients, then use injectivity to kill the $f_i$ coefficients; spanning follows by lifting an element's image in the quotient and subtracting it.

source.place: first displayed sequence and second paragraph, choice and lifting of the g_j and differential basis

proof.text: Let $u=(f_1,\ldots,f_c,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ on this affine neighbourhood of $x$. It is a morphism to $\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$, and its coordinate differentials form the basis of step 3. Apply [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] with $d=c+m$: $X$ is smooth, this neighbourhood is finite type, and the point is $x$. Restrict to the supplied open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ on which $u$ is etale. The equality of ideals from step 2 restricts to $U$, so the ideal of $V=Z\cap U$ is still $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$.

source.place: second paragraph, differential criterion and etale shrinking

proof.text: The coordinate subspace $\mathbf A^m_k\subseteq\mathbf A^{c+m}_k$ has ideal $(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Pulling back its equations gives the ideal $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$, which is exactly the ideal of $V$ by step 4. On each affine open of $U$ the two closed subschemes have the same quotient ring, so $V=U\times_{\mathbf A^{c+m}_k}\mathbf A^m_k=Z\times_XU$ scheme-theoretically. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], the map $u|_V:V\to\mathbf A^m_k$ is etale. The inclusions $U\to X$ and $V\to Z$ are open immersions, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]; they contain $x$ and $z$. These give the claimed etale neighbourhoods and ideal generators for the originally arbitrary point $z$.

source.place: second paragraph, coordinate-subspace inverse image, base change and neighbourhood conclusion

proof_origin.place: complete conormal-coordinate proof, expanded at arbitrary points

split_report.blueprint: Realizes the complete two-paragraph blueprint proof: regular-smooth criterion in step 1, regular generators and conormal basis in step 2, conormal sequence and g_j differential basis in step 3, chosen-coordinate etaleness in step 4, and the linear pair and etale restriction in step 5. The source first works at closed points; the identical differential argument works at every point using the cited rank theorem.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses the existing perfect-field regular-smooth criterion; the model-purity unit has no replacement for this geometric input.
Step 2 uses Hilbert basis to make the affine defining ideal finite and writes the shrinking argument explicitly.
Step 2 uses the existing regular-sequence basis theorem for the defining conormal module.
Step 3 uses the rank of smooth differentials to obtain precisely m coordinate functions, a generic geometry tool not supplied by the model-purity unit.
Step 3 identifies affine differentials with their germs in the cotangent fibre.

lean.statement: theorem regularImmersionLinearization (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (hX : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsSeparated hX] [LocallyOfFiniteType hX] [QuasiCompact hX] [IsSeparated (i ≫ hX)] [LocallyOfFiniteType (i ≫ hX)] [QuasiCompact (i ≫ hX)] [IsClosedImmersion i] (c : ℕ) (hreg : IsRegularImmersionOfPureCodimension hX i c) [Smooth hX] (hZreg : ∀ z : Z, ∃ W : Z.affineOpens, z ∈ W.1 ∧ IsRegularRing Γ(Z, W.1)) : Smooth (i ≫ hX) ∧ ∀ (z : Z), ∃ (m : ℕ), topologicalKrullDimAt z = (m : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ ∃ (U V : Scheme.{u}) (uU : U ⟶ X) (vV : V ⟶ Z) (vU : V ⟶ U) (u : U ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (c + m))) (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k))) (w : V ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k))), Etale uU ∧ Etale vV ∧ Etale u ∧ Etale w ∧ u ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (c + m))) (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) = uU ≫ hX ∧ (∃ zu : U, uU zu = i z ∧ IsIso (uU.residueFieldMap zu)) ∧ (∃ zv : V, vV zv = z ∧ IsIso (vV.residueFieldMap zv)) ∧ IsPullback vU vV uU i ∧ IsPullback vU w u (AffineSpace.homOfVector (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin m)) (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) (fun r : ULift.{u} (Fin (c + m)) ↦ Fin.addCases (fun _ : Fin c ↦ 0) (fun s : Fin m ↦ AffineSpace.coord (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) (ULift.up s)) r.down)) ∧ vU.ker = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop (Ideal.span (Set.range (fun r : Fin c ↦ u.appTop (AffineSpace.coord (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k)) (ULift.up (Fin.castAdd m r))))))
